revenueMix.detail: onX SOS rescue subscription ($49.99 a year, launched July 2026), onX for Business, and brand partnerships (Ford, Toyota, T-Mobile).

onX.mixNote: No percentages published. Nearly all revenue is consumer subscriptions, and Hunt is understood to be the largest app.

current: Expanding onX Fish to more states and to Android
onX SOS in-app emergency rescue, rolling out across the apps
Satellite connectivity through T-Mobile and Starlink
Automaker partnerships: Ford owner bundle, Toyota trail restoration program
Putting the Nov 2025 TCV investment to work
future: Scaling the four activity apps and the user base with TCV, which backed Strava, Netflix and Spotify
More add-on revenue on top of the map subscription (SOS is the first)
No public financial targets

onX.layoffNote: No layoffs found in news, WARN filings or hiring trackers. Headcount looks flat to slightly up over the past two years.

why: Subscription revenue that nearly tripled in three years, described by its investors as profitable
Fresh growth capital from TCV in Nov 2025 and no layoffs found
Marked down for being small and private with no published finances, reliance on discretionary outdoor spending, and rivals bundling free maps (Garmin with HuntStand, automakers)

interest.text: Sells app subscriptions. No lending or financial products.

defense.text: Consumer outdoor-recreation maps. No military or defense customers found; one business directory files it under aerospace and defense only because it makes GPS software.
